donnees.titre: Determining the Quality of Functional Evidence for Coding Variants in CYP1B1 for Use in Variant Classification.
donnees.resume: Biallelic variants in the CYP1B1 gene are associated with primary congenital glaucoma and some instances of anterior segment dysgenesis and juvenile open-angle glaucoma. Genetic testing is increasingly used in the diagnosis of these conditions and to inform future family planning decisions. Variant-specific functional data play a critical role in variant classification during the interpretation of genetic test results. In this study, the ClinGen Glaucoma Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) evaluated published functional assays assessing CYP1B1 protein stability and enzymatic activity to determine which assays meet the recommended standards for use in variant classification, specifically when applying the PS3 or BS3 criteria from the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines. Following a comprehensive literature review, the panel identified assays that examined protein abundance and stability, as well as enzymatic activity across a range of substrates. The VCEP determined that BS3 (benign functional evidence) should not be applied to CYP1B1 as variants exhibit substrate-specific effects. After detailed review, the panel determined that two assays had an adequate number of validation controls and could distinguish between pathogenic and benign variants. The first measured 17β-estradiol activity using a commercially available luminescence kit in yeast microsomes. The second assessed benzo[a]pyrene activity via HPLC detection, also in yeast microsomes. A consensus review of additional assays recommends the inclusion of more clinical controls to either establish a significant OddsPath or to better define thresholds for applying pathogenic evidence. Incorporating validated functional data into the curation of CYP1B1 variants will enhance the accuracy of variant classification.
